1.why: The visible text uses a clean, legible sans-serif with generous vertical whitespace and letter-spaced headings, though it is a generic typeface rather than one specifically designed for dyslexia-friendly reading.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; every visible string is a short title-case or sentence-case line.

3.why: The narrow centred single column would read fine at mobile width, but both headings display raw unrendered Unicode escape text instead of icons, which undermines readability of the content.

4.why: The only guidance on screen is one plain sentence about simulation logs; no actual instructions for the enrolment task are provided at all.

5.why: There are no input fields and no example of expected input shown on either screen.

6.why: The page contains only a few short lines, so the user is never required to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: No codes or secrets are displayed and no copy-to-clipboard control exists, so nothing can be copied instead of typed.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on either screen.

9.why: The page contains no form fields whatsoever, so browser autofill and password managers have nothing to fill.

10.why: Neither screen shows a step indicator or any primary action; both steps display the same static page with only a 'Ready.' log line.

11.why: The user is asked for no action at all (zero buttons or inputs), so it is not true that one main action is requested at a time.

12.why: The only feedback is a static 'Ready.' log line; nothing confirms what happened after an action or explains what comes next.

13.why: There are no retry, reveal/hide, or re-request controls because no code entry step exists in the observed flow.

14.why: No error messages appear anywhere in the observed screens, so none state the problem and the fix.

15.why: No timer or time limit is visible on the static page, but because no code-entry field exists, generous time to enter codes is not actually provided.
